### Sweet Talk
Author: Arlene Pellicane
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-february-13-2020.html
Passage: Ephesians 4:29
Points:
- The Greek term for unwholesome words evokes decaying matter, underscoring how destructive corrupt speech is.
- Growing familiar with loved ones can tempt people toward critical, complaining, or nagging language.
- Believers must evaluate whether their words serve to build others up or tear them down.
- Speaking with grace requires prioritizing the actual needs of others over selfish impulses.
- Setting a guard over one's mouth requires ongoing discipline, patience, and intentional effort.

### Use Your Words to Build Others Up
Author: Rick Warren
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-hope-with-rick-warren/use-your-words-to-build-others-up-daily-hope-with-rick-warren-may-20-2019.html
Passage: Ephesians 4:29
Points:
- Spoken words act like a power tool that can easily demolish relationships if used carelessly.
- Reckless speech inflicts deep wounds that people often remember for decades.
- Believers must stop excusing thoughtless remarks and practice the discipline of speaking less.
- Listening carefully helps identify the real needs and struggles of those around us.
- God calls His followers to use their speech intentionally to encourage and edify others.

### The Liberating Power of Forgiveness
Author: Clarence L. Haynes Jr.
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/the-liberating-power-of-forgiveness-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Ephesians 4:32
Points:
- Harboring unforgiveness inflicts the greatest damage on the person holding the grudge.
- Choosing to forgive does not excuse wrongdoing, but it liberates the soul from bitterness.
- Christ set the supreme example of mercy by forgiving his tormentors while dying on the cross.
- Recognizing the immense debt of sin God forgave in us removes any ground for self-righteousness.
- Extending grace releases anger and paves the way for emotional healing and possible reconciliation.

### Think It Over
Author: Pastor Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living Ministries
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/individual/think-it-over-11
Passage: Ephesians 4:32
Points:
- True personal freedom requires taking the deliberate step to forgive rather than clinging to misery.
- Enduring deep hurt makes it difficult to humble oneself, yet forgiveness remains essential.
- Jesus modeled total surrender to the Father's will by offering forgiveness at Calvary without looking back.
- Believers are commanded to extend tenderhearted kindness because God has already extended forgiveness to them in Christ.
